Sentence (English): I love my new dishwasher !
Comments (English): [ Love my new dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || I love my new dishwasher ! It gets my dishes really clean without hand rinsing. I'm amazed at the amount if soiled kitchenware I get in it. This really cuts down on cleanup time. I love the top rack for utensils and small items, and havin the the middle rack to load medium size items allows more room in the bottom rack for larger items. Cons : the Normal cycles can take up to 3 or 4 hours. This is way too long. I use the express wash almost exclusively and it gets the dishes clean. The door is very heavy to push down to load the dishwasher. I have a bad back and this is difficult for me. I have been using the powdered dishwasher detergent in my other dishwasher in an effort to reduce the use of plastic in pods and plastic containers. I tried it in the new machine and the detergent door would not shut, so I'm stuck using pods or liquid. This is a big deal to me . I want to do my part to protect the environment.

Comments (English): [ Paid on November 27, 2023 and 28 ] || ---------------- || I bought a dishwasher that I paid for on November 27, 2023, installed on the 28th, and am currently using. It has fewer functions than many other products (no automatic door opening function), but I still bought it with the belief that LG is an electronic product. Occasionally I heard a beeping sound during use, but it went away because the frequency of use was low. Since the beginning of January, the sound has been getting longer and longer, and I thought it would get better, but eventually I applied for AS on January 8th. On that day, it was unusable due to the high-frequency sound that gave me a headache. The article visited on January 10th and the motor that sprays water is broken. The original service period for replacing the motor is 1 year, but there is a way to extend it for another year. After hearing the reply that the exchange would not be possible because it had been over a month, I called customer service again and then called the head office. Head office says it's a problem with the pump, not the motor. It's not a cheap home appliance, and the product has a motor or pump problem within a month, so they ask me to fix it and use it. For example, if you were asked to fix a broken engine in a new car, who would do it? If it is a consumable failure, I will understand it again and again. I get angry every time I see the dishwasher in the kitchen.

That's horrible customer service GE !

Sentence (English): My dishwasher died and I ordered a replacement on 12/9 and unfortunately could not be installed until 12/26.
Comments (English): [ Deliver/install process a dumpster fire ] || ---------------- || My dishwasher died and I ordered a replacement on 12/9 and unfortunately could not be installed until 12/26. I later received notice that the dishwasher had shipped on 12/19 and tracking information showed it had made it to Wisconsin so things seemed to be going ok. Within a day or so received a note from Handy that they would be doing installation and that they would be finding a pro. On 12/25, a message from Handy said that the pro cancelled at the last minute and that I was rescheduled for 12/28. On 12/27, I got the same message postponing to Jan 2. Doing dishes by hand over the holidays with guests was getting old. On Jan received note that my contractor cancelled again, and my installation was rescheduled for Jan 5. After the holiday, I called Handy and was told they definitely would have someone out on Jan 5 for sure. On that day, I received an email from Costco apologizing that they could not deliver on intended date and that I needed to schedule. After talking to Costco, they set up a new appt for me on Jan 17th and assured me that everything would be OK. On Jan 4th, the same message from Handy rescheduling to Jan 9. This time, unlike the other times, there was contractor name in the Handy so hoped for the best. Then I got a second message from Costco Direct saying the same thing as before. They said that they could not deliver Dec 26 and they wanted me to get online and set up a new date. I got online and found that the earliest time for delivery was now Jan 26th so I took it although they told me it was Jan 17th before. I got a notice from Handy Jan 8 that my contractor was arriving the next day. I typed a note in the Handy app to the contractor that I did not have a dishwasher yet, but got no response. Then it got creepy. On Jan 9, I received a note that my contractor was on the way. Within an hour, it said "I have arrived" in the message app. I looked for a car but there was no one at my house. I next received a message from Handy a little later saying "My contractor is almost done" And finally I received a note saying the work was completed and to provide an evaluation of the pro. As of Jan 12, I don't know where my dishwasher is or if it will ever arrive. Maybe it will arrive on the 17th, or the 26th and Handy will show up . I have my doubts. Maybe someone will read this and try to help.

Sentence (English): The dishwasher is OK.
Comments (English): [ Take the Bad with the Good. ] || ---------------- || The dishwasher is OK. It has some drawbacks. The biggest drawback is the way most of the space on the inside is made for a specific size and shape of dish. The prongs on the bottom rack that are intended for plates are slanted to the side, meaning it can really only hold plates. When I put my large water goblets there, they simply tip over. With half the bottom rack dedicated to plates (with the plates slots spaced too closely together to use for much else) the remaining space is limited. There's a silverware basket there, which I've resorted to removing, to try to make space for more dishes. It's difficult to put in a large frying pan without crowding in on the plates. The very top rack is for silverware and utensils. It is pushed absolutley up to the top of the interior, so that if you try to set a spatula, carving knife, etc., on its side for proper washing, it is knocked over when you try to pull the door open or closed. Forks and knives that do fit have to be painstakingly layed into the little slits--and again, the slits vary in size so that many things only fit in one particular slit--so good luck if you have more than a couple of a particular item. You could use the silverware basket on the lower rack, but of course then you won't have room for all of your dishes. I was excited to have the little holder for stemware, (middle rack) until I found that it will only accomodate a very narrow \"stem\", like would be on a chamagne flute, etc. My water goblets, that we use for everything, did not fit there after all. The goblets also would not even fit standing up, until I lowered the middle rack as far as it would go. This will ultimately interfere with any \"tall\" things that I want to wash on the bottom. And again, with the middle rack, the majority of the prongs on the rack are slanted, meaning things have to face a certain way, and you have to brace tall items against other things so that they won't just flop over. Very frustrating. Places to stand things properly upright are very limited, and this rack has to be used on it's lowest setting, or it's simply too narrow for many things. A very problematic thing is that there is no \"full\" indicator on the rinse-aid dispenser. As near as I can tell, you have to guess as to when it's time to add. And then when you do, the rinse aid simply runs out the cracks of--and out the bottom of-- the dispenser. Is it defective? I don't know. It's been like this since day-one. There is no section of the owner's manual addressing this. And forget about the \"crystal dry\" setting. Are the dishes drier than they were with the old washer? Sentence (English): The dishwasher is OK.
Comments (English): [ Take the Bad with the Good. ] || ---------------- || The dishwasher is OK. It has some drawbacks. The biggest drawback is the way most of the space on the inside is made for a specific size and shape of dish. The prongs on the bottom rack that are intended for plates are slanted to the side, meaning it can really only hold plates. When I put my large water goblets there, they simply tip over. With half the bottom rack dedicated to plates (with the plates slots spaced too closely together to use for much else) the remaining space is limited. There's a silverware basket there, which I've resorted to removing, to try to make space for more dishes. It's difficult to put in a large frying pan without crowding in on the plates.The very top rack is for silverware and utensils. It is pushed absolutley up to the top of the interior, so that if you try to set a spatula, carving knife, etc., on its side for proper washing, it is knocked over when you try to pull the door open or closed. Forks and knives that do fit have to be painstakingly layed into the little slits--and again, the slits vary in size so that many things only fit in one particular slit--so good luck if you have more than a couple of a particular item. You could use the silverware basket on the lower rack, but of course then you won't have room for all of your dishes. I was excited to have the little holder for stemware, (middle rack) until I found that it will only accomodate a very narrow "stem", like would be on a chamagne flute, etc. My water goblets, that we use for everything, did not fit there after all. The goblets also would not even fit standing up, until I lowered the middle rack as far as it would go. This will ultimately interfere with any "tall" things that I want to wash on the bottom. And again, with the middle rack, the majority of the prongs on the rack are slanted, meaning things have to face a certain way, and you have to brace tall items against other things so that they won't just flop over. Very frustrating. Places to stand things properly upright are very limited, and this rack has to be used on it's lowest setting, or it's simply too narrow for many things.A very problematic thing is that there is no "full" indicator on the rinse-aid dispenser. As near as I can tell, you have to guess as to when it's time to add. And then when you do, the rinse aid simply runs out the cracks of--and out the bottom of-- the dispenser. Is it defective? I don't know. It's been like this since day-one. There is no section of the owner's manual addressing this.And forget about the "crystal dry" setting. Are the dishes drier than they were with the old washer? Yeah, but there are still water droplets on many dishes and of course puddles inside of all the nooks and crannies where the water can't drain away. Nothing is dry as a bone.The dishes come out clean enough, but you'll still have to rewash the frying pans and deep kettles as usual. Would I buy it again? Maybe. But first I would look for a dishwasher with straight up-and-down prongs on its racks, (spaced a little farther apart) so that I could put what I want, where I want, without my tall glasses falling over and without the interior space being so cut-up, specialized, and compartmentalized that it severely limits how you load it. In the end, despite having three racks instead of two, this dishwasher holds fewer dishes.

The biggest drawback is the way most of the space on the inside is made for a specific size and shape of dish. The prongs on the bottom rack that are intended for plates are slanted to the side, meaning it can really only hold plates. When I put my large water goblets there, they simply tip over. With half the bottom rack dedicated to plates (with the plates slots spaced too closely together to use for much else) the remaining space is limited. There's a silverware basket there, which I've resorted to removing, to try to make space for more dishes. It's difficult to put in a large frying pan without crowding in on the plates.The very top rack is for silverware and utensils. It is pushed absolutley up to the top of the interior, so that if you try to set a spatula, carving knife, etc., on its side for proper washing, it is knocked over when you try to pull the door open or closed. Forks and knives that do fit have to be painstakingly layed into the little slits--and again, the slits vary in size so that many things only fit in one particular slit--so good luck if you have more than a couple of a particular item. You could use the silverware basket on the lower rack, but of course then you won't have room for all of your dishes. I was excited to have the little holder for stemware, (middle rack) until I found that it will only accomodate a very narrow "stem", like would be on a chamagne flute, etc. My water goblets, that we use for everything, did not fit there after all. The goblets also would not even fit standing up, until I lowered the middle rack as far as it would go. This will ultimately interfere with any "tall" things that I want to wash on the bottom. And again, with the middle rack, the majority of the prongs on the rack are slanted, meaning things have to face a certain way, and you have to brace tall items against other things so that they won't just flop over. Very frustrating. Places to stand things properly upright are very limited, and this rack has to be used on it's lowest setting, or it's simply too narrow for many things.A very problematic thing is that there is no "full" indicator on the rinse-aid dispenser. As near as I can tell, you have to guess as to when it's time to add. And then when you do, the rinse aid simply runs out the cracks of--and out the bottom of-- the dispenser. Is it defective? I don't know. It's been like this since day-one. There is no section of the owner's manual addressing this.And forget about the "crystal dry" setting. Are the dishes drier than they were with the old washer? Yeah, but there are still water droplets on many dishes and of course puddles inside of all the nooks and crannies where the water can't drain away. Nothing is dry as a bone.The dishes come out clean enough, but you'll still have to rewash the frying pans and deep kettles as usual. Would I buy it again? Maybe. But first I would look for a dishwasher with straight up-and-down prongs on its racks, (spaced a little farther apart) so that I could put what I want, where I want, without my tall glasses falling over and without the interior space being so cut-up, specialized, and compartmentalized that it severely limits how you load it. In the end, despite having three racks instead of two, this dishwasher holds fewer dishes.

The prongs on the bottom rack that are intended for plates are slanted to the side, meaning it can really only hold plates. When I put my large water goblets there, they simply tip over. With half the bottom rack dedicated to plates (with the plates slots spaced too closely together to use for much else) the remaining space is limited. There's a silverware basket there, which I've resorted to removing, to try to make space for more dishes. It's difficult to put in a large frying pan without crowding in on the plates.The very top rack is for silverware and utensils. It is pushed absolutley up to the top of the interior, so that if you try to set a spatula, carving knife, etc., on its side for proper washing, it is knocked over when you try to pull the door open or closed. Forks and knives that do fit have to be painstakingly layed into the little slits--and again, the slits vary in size so that many things only fit in one particular slit--so good luck if you have more than a couple of a particular item. You could use the silverware basket on the lower rack, but of course then you won't have room for all of your dishes. I was excited to have the little holder for stemware, (middle rack) until I found that it will only accomodate a very narrow "stem", like would be on a chamagne flute, etc. My water goblets, that we use for everything, did not fit there after all. The goblets also would not even fit standing up, until I lowered the middle rack as far as it would go. This will ultimately interfere with any "tall" things that I want to wash on the bottom. And again, with the middle rack, the majority of the prongs on the rack are slanted, meaning things have to face a certain way, and you have to brace tall items against other things so that they won't just flop over. Very frustrating. Places to stand things properly upright are very limited, and this rack has to be used on it's lowest setting, or it's simply too narrow for many things.A very problematic thing is that there is no "full" indicator on the rinse-aid dispenser. As near as I can tell, you have to guess as to when it's time to add. And then when you do, the rinse aid simply runs out the cracks of--and out the bottom of-- the dispenser. Is it defective? I don't know. It's been like this since day-one. There is no section of the owner's manual addressing this.And forget about the "crystal dry" setting. Are the dishes drier than they were with the old washer? Yeah, but there are still water droplets on many dishes and of course puddles inside of all the nooks and crannies where the water can't drain away. But first I would look for a dishwasher with straight up-and-down prongs on its racks, (spaced a little farther apart) so that I could put what I want, where I want, without my tall glasses falling over and without the interior space being so cut-up, specialized, and compartmentalized that it severely limits how you load it. Yeah, but there are still water droplets on many dishes and of course puddles inside of all the nooks and crannies where the water can't drain away.  Nothing is dry as a bone.The dishes come out clean enough, but you'll still have to rewash the frying pans and deep kettles as usual.  Would I buy it again?  Maybe.  But first I would look for a dishwasher  with straight up-and-down prongs on its racks, (spaced a little farther apart) so that I could put what I want, where I want, without my tall glasses falling over and without the interior space being so cut-up, specialized, and compartmentalized that it severely limits how you load it.  In the end, despite having three racks instead of two, this dishwasher holds fewer dishes.

Sentence (English): I paid on November 27, 2023, installed on the 28th, and am using the dishwasher.
Comments (English): I paid on November 27, 2023, installed on the 28th, and am using the dishwasher. It has fewer functions than many other products (no automatic door opening function), but I still bought it because I believed that LG is the best for electronic products. I occasionally heard a beeping sound while using it, but it just passed because I didn't use it often. Since the beginning of January, the sound time has gotten longer and longer, and I thought it would get better, but I finally received AS on January 8th. On that day, it was impossible to use due to the high-frequency sound that gave me a headache. On January 10th, a technician visited and the motor that sprays water was broken. I replaced the motor and the service was originally for one year, but there was a way to extend it for another year. Since it had been over a month, I was told that it would not be exchanged, so I called the customer service center again and called the head office. The head office said that it was not a problem with the motor, but with the pump. It's not a cheap home appliance, and they told me to fix a product with a problem with the motor or pump in less than a month. For example, who would pay for a new car with a broken engine and tell me to fix it? If it's a consumable failure, I can accept it no matter how many times I look at the dishwasher in the kitchen.
Comments (Original): 2023년11월27일에 결재하고 28일인가 설치하고 사용중인 식기세척기, 다수의 여러제품보다 기능이 적지만(자동 문열림 기능 없음) 그래도 역시 전자제품은 LG 라는 믿음으로 구입했다. 사용중에 가끔 “삐익” 거리는 소리가 들렸으나 사용빈도가 낮아 그냥 지났다. 1월초부터 점점 소리의 시간이 길어졌고 괜찮아 지겠지 하다가 결국 1월8일 AS 접수했다. 그날은 두통이 날 정도의 고주파 소리로 사용이 불가한 상황이다. 1월10일 기사 방문하여“ 물을 쏴주는 모터가 고장이다. 모터를 갈고 서비스가 원래 1년인데 1년 더 연장하는 방법이 있다.” 한 달이 넘었기 때문에 교환은 안 될거다, 라는 답변을 듣고 고객센터에 다시 전화를 했고 본사까지 통화를 했다. 본사는 모터가 아니라 펌프의 이상이란다. 싼 가격의 가전제품도 아니고 한달도 안되서 모터나 펌프의 이상이 있는 제품을 나더러 고쳐서 쓰란다. 예를 들어보자 새차에 엔진 고장난 걸 고쳐서 쓰라고 하면 누가 납들을 할까? 소모품 고장이라면 몇 번이고 납득하겠다.주방에 있는 세척기 볼 때 마다 화가 치밀어 오른다.

Sentence (English): Coming home from work, doing housework, and the repetitive routine was so tiresome that I wanted to escape the daily grind of washing dishes.
Comments (English): [ I was tired of the repetitive routine of coming home from work, doing housework, and doing the dishes, so I wanted to escape and buy a dishwasher, but since I live in a rented studio apartment, I decided that an installed type would be too much of a hassle, so I bought a non-installed dishwasher. ] || ---------------- || Coming home from work, doing housework, and the repetitive routine was so tiresome that I wanted to escape the daily grind of washing dishes. I was considering buying a dishwasher, but since I live in a studio apartment, I decided a stand-alone dishwasher wouldn't be feasible, so I ended up buying a stand-alone dishwasher. While debating which one to buy, I came across a YouTube video. Among the small, stand-alone dishwashers for 1-2 people, the Chefbone seemed to have the widest interior and cleanest style, so I ordered it. First, I added detergent without any dishes and ran it once, then added the dishes on the second run. Warm water came out and the dishes were washed cleanly. I used the water tank I had at home, but the 3L capacity was small, so I had to refill it two or three times. Additionally, there was a slight unpleasant odor when drying the dishes after washing them, so I recommend turning it off and leaving the door open to dry them. If this bothers you, I recommend considering this option. If you live alone in a studio apartment and don't want to bother with dishes, I recommend the Washpoll 4.

I have had dishwashers the last 40 years of my life and I've never had one that doesn't tell you by some kind of light on the outside or even when you open it up to say “clean”. To say that you can tell if you can't open the drawer is not a good way to tell because I have been able to open it whether or not it's still running or not and then you have to start the cycle over again. I am quite sure if I knew this about this dishwasher I would not have purchased it so buyer beware!

Sentence (English): This Samsung dishwasher is suitable for beginners.
Comments (English): [ Suitable for beginners of dishwashing ] || ---------------- || This Samsung dishwasher is suitable for beginners. It has the exact same frame as the Chinese-made ones, but I chose it because I was afraid of self-installation. If you arrange the dishes diagonally like Tetris (it's difficult at first), ceramic items dry perfectly, and plastics dry about 80%. Of course, what gets cleaned comes out spotlessly clean. As for detergent, I completely ignored German brands and used the small size of Natural Pong. Both the Quick and Regular cycles dissolve detergents well and have great cleaning power. I think it would be perfect if I switched to the model with hot air drying after using it for a few years.
Comments (Original): [ 식세기 입문용으로 적당 ] || ---------------- || 식세기 입문할때 적당한 삼성식기세척기입니다.중국발 프레임이랑 똑같은데 자가설치 무서움 때문에 산택했구요식기 비스듬하게 테트리스(처음엔어려움) 하면 도기류는 완벽하고 플라스틱류는 80%전도 건조됩니다.물론 닦이는건 깨끗하게 닦이구요.세제는 독일제 이런거 다 개무시하고  자연퐁 작게나온거 썼습니다.쾌속, 정주행 둘다 잘녹이고 세척략 좋아요.한 몇년 써보고 열풍으로 건조되는거 쓰면 완벽할꺼 같네요.

Comments (English): [ Great dishwasher. Wrote my backorder experience. ] || ---------------- || I've used the dishwasher for 2 weeks and I love it so far. Before ordering, the online estimate said 11/5, but after ordering I saw an additional estimate of 12/21. It also mentioned if the order takes longer than 30 days it will be automatically canceled. I went in store to see if they had further information, but they didn't. I later did an online chat support, they also didn't have further information but assured me my order would not be canceled (not sure if that was because I asked for it to not be canceled or just a normal fact). Then on 12/21, the second estimated date that had sinced dissappeared from record, I recieved an email that it had arrived. It could be a coincidence, but in my experience I think that second estimate is the real date and hopefully Best Buy software engineers are working on fixing how their backorders display dates.

This crew pulled everything out from under the sink and said that the dishwasher we bought wouldn't fit. Proceeded to measure the cutout as 1 & 1/2" too short, took photos and left. A dozen phone calls and 2 weeks later I installed it myself and asked to have the install refunded and discount applied for the damage done to the brand new appliance.

Sentence (English): Although I have only been able to use it once, the results of the dishwasher have been very satisfactory.

Here is a comparison to our previous machine:1. First and foremost, Bosch has spent significant resources in intelligently creating instructions and instructional videos on how to use their machine most effectively. I have found these resources immensely useful and it's something that our previous machine manufacturer have clearly not prioritized. It demonstrates a focus on the customer (rather than just sales).2. Trays: The upper "tray" is WAY more useful and feature friendly than our previous machine. This is an aspect that Bosch doesn't seem to play up enough. It's a huge differentiator. The upper "rack" is well designed and I have found it more useful than my previous machine. The lower "rack" has room for improvement. The tines in the lower rack are way too narrow for ANY of my dishes. This makes for awkward and inefficient loading and a worry that the tines will get bent over time. Bosch needs to consider at the very least selling a lower rack with wider spaced tines as a replacement or option. I did not have this problem with my previous machine (much less so anyway).3. Space: Dishwashers are essentially all the same size and shape. Yet somehow the lower rack on the Bosch appears to be able to accommodate fewer items. This might have to do with where the operating parts of the machine reside (behind or under the machine). I'm not 100% sure of this but I think the Bosch has taller inside dimensions while my previous machine had deeper inside dimensions. My previous machine had a food grinder while the Bosch uses a filter - this may account for some of that difference. Also no heating elements on the Bosch while my previous machine had heating elements.4. Washing: cleans everything brilliantly. However, my previous machine did too for the 1st year. Then things started to not work so well. So the jury is still out on my Bosch which I have only had for a couple months now.5. Hard Water Treatment: The Bosch offers the ability to treat hard water based on water hardness in your municipality. This appears to have made a huge difference in managing residue. Somehow my dishes come out a lot cleaner with a little hard water management than they did without (I tried with and without in the same Bosh machine and found with hard water management there was a significant improvement).6. Noise: This machine is markedly noisier than my previous machine. Not a deal breaker, but noteworthy.7. Drying: I find that it does a good job of it, but even at maximum settings, water puddles at the top of coffee mugs and such. So one really has to make an effort to put items in the machine at an angle as much as possible. In my opinion, Bosch should tweak it's racks so that coffee mugs and other items with flat but indented bottoms sit at more of an angle. Additionally, I find that the spray arms have water in them so if you happen to even nudge them, they drip water all over the clean dishes. I did not have this problem with my previous machine. Not a deal breaker, but worth noting.8. Jet Dry Reservoir: No visual indicator of levels. You have to rely on the sensor and and on screen display to tell you it's low. The sensor has to date not come on, so it makes me uneasy. As a result I keep filling it, just in case. My previous machine had a window where you could see the level.9. Smart/App tools. These work well and are easy to configure. I can only shudder at the thought of how badly my previous machine's manufacturer would have botched that aspect. Bosch has done a good job with it. Again demonstrates customer focus.10. Load in progress indicator: The red light indicator on the floor that the machine is running is a neat feature and is a value add.Overall, I am happy with this new machine, but it is way too early to really write a conclusive review on it. If Costco/Bosch pestered me for a review 3 years after purchase rather than immediately after, this review may have had more value. No matter the features, if a machine dies in 3 years, it's a piece of junk.

Here is a comparison to our previous machine:1. First and foremost, Bosch has spent significant resources in intelligently creating instructions and instructional videos on how to use their machine most effectively. I have found these resources immensely useful and it's something that our previous machine manufacturer have clearly not prioritized. It demonstrates a focus on the customer (rather than just sales).2. Trays: The upper "tray" is WAY more useful and feature friendly than our previous machine. This is an aspect that Bosch doesn't seem to play up enough. It's a huge differentiator. The upper "rack" is well designed and I have found it more useful than my previous machine. The lower "rack" has room for improvement. The tines in the lower rack are way too narrow for ANY of my dishes. This makes for awkward and inefficient loading and a worry that the tines will get bent over time. Bosch needs to consider at the very least selling a lower rack with wider spaced tines as a replacement or option. I did not have this problem with my previous machine (much less so anyway).3. Space: Dishwashers are essentially all the same size and shape. Yet somehow the lower rack on the Bosch appears to be able to accommodate fewer items. This might have to do with where the operating parts of the machine reside (behind or under the machine). I'm not 100% sure of this but I think the Bosch has taller inside dimensions while my previous machine had deeper inside dimensions. My previous machine had a food grinder while the Bosch uses a filter - this may account for some of that difference. Also no heating elements on the Bosch while my previous machine had heating elements.4. Washing: cleans everything brilliantly. However, my previous machine did too for the 1st year. Then things started to not work so well. So the jury is still out on my Bosch which I have only had for a couple months now.5. Hard Water Treatment: The Bosch offers the ability to treat hard water based on water hardness in your municipality. This appears to have made a huge difference in managing residue. Somehow my dishes come out a lot cleaner with a little hard water management than they did without (I tried with and without in the same Bosh machine and found with hard water management there was a significant improvement).6. Noise: This machine is markedly noisier than my previous machine. Not a deal breaker, but noteworthy.7. Drying: I find that it does a good job of it, but even at maximum settings, water puddles at the top of coffee mugs and such. So one really has to make an effort to put items in the machine at an angle as much as possible. In my opinion, Bosch should tweak it's racks so that coffee mugs and other items with flat but indented bottoms sit at more of an angle. Additionally, I find that the spray arms have water in them so if you happen to even nudge them, they drip water all over the clean dishes. I did not have this problem with my previous machine. Not a deal breaker, but worth noting.8. Jet Dry Reservoir: No visual indicator of levels. You have to rely on the sensor and and on screen display to tell you it's low. The sensor has to date not come on, so it makes me uneasy. As a result I keep filling it, just in case. My previous machine had a window where you could see the level.9. Smart/App tools. These work well and are easy to configure. I can only shudder at the thought of how badly my previous machine's manufacturer would have botched that aspect. Bosch has done a good job with it. Again demonstrates customer focus.10. Load in progress indicator: The red light indicator on the floor that the machine is running is a neat feature and is a value add.Overall, I am happy with this new machine, but it is way too early to really write a conclusive review on it. If Costco/Bosch pestered me for a review 3 years after purchase rather than immediately after, this review may have had more value. No matter the features, if a machine dies in 3 years, it's a piece of junk.

Sentence (English): DO NOT BUY THIS IF YOU WANT CLEAN DISHES!
Comments (English): [ Doesn't clean the dishes ] || ---------------- || DO NOT BUY THIS IF YOU WANT CLEAN DISHES! I've had this dishwasher for 3 months. Got a b6 code (which means there's too many suds) and the dishwasher stopped mid-wash the first time I used it even though I was using the regular dishwasher pod I used with my prior non-LG machine. Had to go to liquid detergent to get the dishwasher to complete the cycle. But it doesn't matter whether the dishwasher completed the wash or not. It doesn't remove food from the dishes. Even if I eat a bowl of ice cream and put it right into the dishwasher and start it, it won't wash off the fresh liquid ice cream! never had this happen before. Tried having my plumber increase my water pressure, but that didn't help. I know the jets are running because when I open it mid-wash there's water all along the inside of the dishwasher. I travel for work a lot and haven't been home enough to deal with this issue. At this point I'm outside the 90 day window to return or exchange to Costco (which is fair since it's been 113 calendar days/78 business days since it was delivered), so am going to be stuck dealing with LG warranty service or with an expensive dishwasher that doesn't wash the dishes. Hopefully Costco will at least help me coordinate with the LG warranty people.

Sentence (English): About 10 years ago, I rented a dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Welcome, Auntie Dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || About 10 years ago, I rented a dishwasher. Then I moved, and there was no place to put it. So, even though I still had a contract left, I had no choice but to return it, paying a penalty. I vowed to myself that next time I'd buy one without a penalty. Finally, I bought my own house and bought a dishwasher. I love this dishwasher again! It's even more powerful than the one I had 10 years ago. It really washes away stuck-on rice. Ten years ago, it sometimes wouldn't wash stuck-on rice, and sometimes it would stay stuck. I used to use Echover detergent, but these days, there are so many different ones. I've tried a variety of products, and Scotch seems pretty good for the price, and Frosch is also good. Samsung is also offering a discount coupon for Echover, so I'm thinking about ordering one too. I thought it was a Wi-Fi model, but I was a little disappointed when I found out it wasn't. Actually, there's nothing to do with Wi-Fi. The only downside is that you can't see the remaining time. The advantage of the built-in is that it's easy to install. Perhaps because of that neatness, the LCD screen to check the remaining time isn't visible from the outside. I was worried because there were a lot of dishes that weren't supposed to be in the dishwasher. Sentence (English): This is my first review of purchasing a dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ This is my first review of purchasing a dishwasher. ] || ---------------- || This is my first review of purchasing a dishwasher. The purchase time was conducted at Best Shop with friendly explanations about dishwashers. The price difference wasn't that much and I liked some discounts, so I decided on a built-in room for 14 people. We prepared the sink after remodeling it with another company, but the installer said it was uninstallable, so we decided to exchange it for a freestanding one that can accommodate 12 people. Although this process seemed to take time, the three-way communication between Best Shop's sales staff and the installation engineer was smooth, so the cancellation and repurchase process was completed smoothly. The next day, luckily, the same installer was assigned. The installation process took some time as there was a jam in the flooring, but fortunately the installation was completed with an emphasis on leveling the product. Although it was a small space, it was possible to install it. There were no additional installation costs. On the first day, I did a tub wash, and the next morning, after stacking the dishes, pots, and spoons in a Tetris pattern, I cut the Prosh All-in-One tablet detergent in half and set it to the standard course and hot air drying for 60 minutes. After completion, it was cleaned smoothly and there were some white water stains, but they were not noticeable. However, there were some food stains left, perhaps because the pot was not completely laid down. I think it will be okay once I have the know-how to arrange the dishes. Since I heard the explanation about using rinse aid and refined salt during installation, I think I will have to try it in the future and compare. I am also participating in a 6-month careship program and am excited to see what it will be like. Dishwashers are expected to reduce dishwashing labor. I believe that LG is the best when it comes to Becksack home appliances and look forward to using it for a long time.
Comments (Original): [ 식기세척기 처음으로 구매해본 후기. ] || ---------------- || 식기세척기 처음으로 구매해본 후기. 베스트샵에서 식기세척기 관련 친절한 설명과 함께 진행했던 구매시간. 가격차이가 얼마나지 않고 몇가지 할인이 좋아서 14인용 빌트인으로 정했음. 싱크장은 다른업체와 개조를 완료하고 준비하였으나 설치기사님 왈 설치불가한 구조이기에 12인용 프리스탠딩으로 교환하기로 함. 이 과정에 시간이 걸리는듯 하였으나 베스트샵 판매직원분과 설치기사님과의 3자소통이 원활하였기에 취소부터 재구매 과정까지 일사천리로 완료. 다음날 운좋게도 같은 설치기사님 배정. 설치과정에서도 장판걸림이 있어서 시간이 소요되긴 했으나 제품의 수평맞춤에 중점을 두고 다행이도 설치까지 완료. 좁은 공간이었지만 설치할수 있었음. 설치비용이 추가로 들지는 않았음. 첫날 통세척을 한번 해주고 다음날 오전 그릇과 냄비 수저 등을 테트리스로 잘 쌓은뒤에 프로쉬올인원 태블릿 세제를 절반으로 잘라서 표준코스와 열풍건조60분으로 함께 설정해서 시작. 완료뒤에는 순조로이 세척이 잘 되었고 약간의 흰 물얼룩이 있으나 개념치 않을 정도였으며, 다만 냄비가 완전히 뉘여져 있지 않아서인지 약간의 음식물 자국이 남아있었음. 그릇배열의 노하우가 생기면 괜찮아지지 않을까 생각함. 설치시 린스사용과 정제소금관련 설명을 들어보았기에 차후에 시도해보면서 비교해야할것같음. 6개월 케어쉽 프로그램도 참여중인데 어떨지 기대가 됨. 설거지 노동이 줄어들것으로 기대되는 식기세척기.벡색가전제품에선 엘지가 가장 좋다는 믿음과 함께 오래오래 사용하길 기대중.

Sentence (English): You will be contacted when you order a dishwasher.

If you need to partially repair or reinstall an existing sink, we recommend recommending a sink company or finding one yourself. If you repair the sink for 1-2 hours and tell the dishwasher installer the schedule, he will calculate the time and come. Sentence (English): A couple of significant problems have made this a frustrating dishwasher to own.
Comments (English): [ Door latch is not secure. ] || ---------------- || A couple of significant problems have made this a frustrating dishwasher to own. Since we first got it (8 months ago), the door latch has never closed securely, causing the door to pop open. So far this has not caused any disasters, but it takes several tries to get the door to stay closed so I can run it. I had warranty service to replace the door latch about 2 months after purchase, and again about 6 months later; we'll see how it goes after the second service. The dishwasher does an adequate but not exceptional job cleaning dishes. I have found that any silverware placed in the silverware holder on the bottom level does not get clean (we always clean off all solid material by prewashing everything before loading). Silverware on the upper rack does get clean, so we use the third rack exclusively and leave the bottom silverware holder empty. Generally I have found that out of each load, 5 or 6 dishes need to be washed by hand after coming out of the dishwasher still dirty. This is regardless of the setting used; even the most powerful setting doesn't get everything clean. We have to fill the upper rack no more than about half full to allow circulation, especially for bowls. The sound level on this dishwasher is approximately 55dB, not 45dB as advertised. It's still fairly quiet.

I also don't like that there isn't a way to check the level of rinse liquid to see if it's low or out.

I think there is a micro switch that senses when the door is closed and allows power, but it's not powering up unless I open and close the door multiple times and unplug and plug in the power cord to the outlet. This is an ongoing issue. Additionally, the pump that drains the dishwasher had the internal impeller blades degraded such that the pump did not drain the water. So, plumber used existing kit and installed the dishwasher. I decided to dispose of the old dishwasher myself at this point, so I called Home Depot and requested a $50 refund for the haul away that I already paid for online. They said sure, but I would have to physically drive to a Home Depot store to receive the $50 refund. You've got to be kidding me, my original order was an online order, Home Depot was happy to take my money, but to get my refund I have to drive to the store? Ridiculous. Plus the whole reason for this is that the original crew had no interest in installing the dishwasher when they certainly could have done so all in one trip.

Sentence (English): I've had this dishwasher about a month now and it replaced a 16 year old KitchenAid which I was very happy with and was why I chose a KitchenAid to replace it.
Comments (English): [ Very quiet with a surprisingly useful third rack ] || ---------------- || I've had this dishwasher about a month now and it replaced a 16 year old KitchenAid which I was very happy with and was why I chose a KitchenAid to replace it. The biggest improvement is the third rack, which is actually very useful and has its own set of sprayers incorporated into the design. The new dishwasher is very quiet and slightly quieter than my old KitchenAid. The cycle time is a bit longer than my old one but the dishes always come out clean. I do have a couple of quibbles: The silverware basket has a slotted top so that you can ostensibly load your silverware standing upright. On this new one, the slots don't always match the partitions in the main basket rendering some of the slots useless. My old one was better in that regard in that the slots lined up with the basket. Another issue is that they included only two tabs to hold stemware glasses which is not enough for my household. My old KitchenAid had fold-down tines that could accommodate up to 8 stemware glasses. Additional stemware tabs can be purchased through Whirlpool parts, but the price is a bit stiff.

Sentence (English): Bought this instead of a similarly priced Bosch 800 to upgrade from a 10 year old Bosch 300, as it seemed to look nicer and didn't have the unnecessary “smart” features like Bosch Homeconnect.
Comments (English): [ Broke twice within the first year ] || ---------------- || Bought this instead of a similarly priced Bosch 800 to upgrade from a 10 year old Bosch 300, as it seemed to look nicer and didn't have the unnecessary “smart” features like Bosch Homeconnect. The dishwasher washes and dries well, however the exposed heating element at the bottom has the power to melt even hard plastics on the bottom shelf. Never had this issue before with dishwashers. The dishwasher also has excellent looks and is easy to use. The third rack is great, especially with the additional sprayer. The dishwasher broke twice within the first year - the door hinges once, and the sealing gasket once. I think the best analogy of this dishwasher is a premium GM product - like a Chevy Tahoe. It's luxurious, looks nice, feels good, more or less reliable primary parts but really junk overall quality and small things constantly breaking (like door locks or window switches or paint scraping off the buttons). If you're ok with minor problems but overall decent performance of the primary parts, this will do. It'll wash your dishes and it'll dry them - but will constantly be in and out of repairs for small things like buttons, door hinges, or gaskets. Overall, I wouldn't recommend it. Once the warranty runs out, and if it breaks again, it may be more economical to just buy a new dishwasher, which certainly won't be a kitchenaid or any other whirlpool brand. My 10 year old Bosch looked and felt better at the 10 year mark than this dishwasher at a 1 year mark.

Sentence (English): I wanted a reliable dishwasher with a third row, and certainly got that.
Comments (English): [ Love it overall! ] || ---------------- || I wanted a reliable dishwasher with a third row, and certainly got that. I love the drying system because there is not a heating element that will melt my plastics and it does not emit steam (my previous dishwasher was damaging the wooden trim original to my house if I used the heat dry). I do not use a rinse aid and glass, metal, and dishes all dry well. Plastics stay pretty wet, but I find that to be true of most dishwashers and don't mind drying those. The inside of the dishwasher does look wet after a cleaning cycle, so I do prop the dishwasher door open between most washes to help everything dry out better. Dishes come out very clean and the dishwasher is very quiet. I don't find it necessary to use the features in the smart app unless I want to delay the start time. I do wish I could do a delayed start without the app, but it's nothing I can't work with. The positioning of the tines on the racks do take a little getting used to, but it didn't take long to figure out how to best load it to maximize space. I've had this model for about 6 weeks, and I am still very pleased with my purchase.

Sentence (English): Bought this instead of a similarly priced Bosch 800 to upgrade from a 10 year old Bosch 300, as it seemed to look nicer and didn't have the unnecessary "smart" features like Bosch Homeconnect.
Comments (English): [ Broke twice within the first year ] || ---------------- || Bought this instead of a similarly priced Bosch 800 to upgrade from a 10 year old Bosch 300, as it seemed to look nicer and didn't have the unnecessary "smart" features like Bosch Homeconnect. The dishwasher washes and dries well, however the exposed heating element at the bottom has the power to melt even hard plastics on the bottom shelf. Never had this issue before with dishwashers. The dishwasher also has excellent looks and is easy to use. The third rack is great, especially with the additional sprayer. The dishwasher broke twice within the first year - the door hinges once, and the sealing gasket once. I think the best analogy of this dishwasher is a premium GM product - like a Chevy Tahoe. Sentence (English): A couple of significant problems have made this a frustrating dishwasher to own.
Comments (English): [ Door latch is not secure. ] || ---------------- || A couple of significant problems have made this a frustrating dishwasher to own.Since we first got it (8 months ago), the door latch has never closed securely, causing the door to pop open. So far this has not caused any disasters, but it takes several tries to get the door to stay closed so I can run it. I had warranty service to replace the door latch about 2 months after purchase, and again about 6 months later; we'll see how it goes after the second service.The dishwasher does an adequate but not exceptional job cleaning dishes. I have found that any silverware placed in the silverware holder on the bottom level does not get clean (we always clean off all solid material by prewashing everything before loading). Silverware on the upper rack does get clean, so we use the third rack exclusively and leave the bottom silverware holder empty. Generally I have found that out of each load, 5 or 6 dishes need to be washed by hand after coming out of the dishwasher still dirty. This is regardless of the setting used; even the most powerful setting doesn't get everything clean. We have to fill the upper rack no more than about half full to allow circulation, especially for bowls.The sound level on this dishwasher is approximately 55dB, not 45dB as advertised. It's still fairly quiet.

Sentence (English): Review of the first dishwasher purchase.
Comments (English): Review of the first dishwasher purchase. Purchase time with friendly explanation about dishwasher at Bestshop. The price difference is not much and there are some good discounts, so I decided to go with a 14-person built-in. The sink was remodeled and prepared with another company, but the installer said that it was not a structure that could be installed, so I decided to exchange it for a 12-person freestanding. This process seemed to take time, but since the Bestshop sales staff and the installer communicated smoothly, the cancellation and repurchase process were completed quickly. The next day, luckily, the same installer was assigned. The installation process also took time because the floorboard was jammed, but fortunately, the installation was completed with a focus on leveling the product. It was possible to install it even though it was a small space. There was no additional installation cost. I washed it once on the first day, and the next morning, I stacked dishes, pots, and spoons with Tetris, cut the Prosh All-in-One tablet detergent in half, set it to the standard course and hot air drying for 60 minutes, and started. After completion, it washed smoothly and there were some white stains, but they were not noticeable. However, there were some food stains because the pot was not completely laid down. I think it will be okay once I get the know-how to arrange the dishes. Since I heard an explanation about the use of rinse aid and refined salt during installation, I think I will have to try it out later and compare. I am also participating in the 6-month care ship program, so I am looking forward to it. A dishwasher that is expected to reduce the amount of work required to wash dishes. I believe that LG is the best in white home appliances and I look forward to using it for a long time.
Comments (Original): 식기세척기 처음으로 구매해본 후기. 베스트샵에서 식기세척기 관련 친절한 설명과 함께 진행했던 구매시간. 가격차이가 얼마나지 않고 몇가지 할인이 좋아서 14인용 빌트인으로 정했음. 싱크장은 다른업체와 개조를 완료하고 준비하였으나 설치기사님 왈 설치불가한 구조이기에 12인용 프리스탠딩으로 교환하기로 함. 이 과정에 시간이 걸리는듯 하였으나 베스트샵 판매직원분과 설치기사님과의 3자소통이 원활하였기에 취소부터 재구매 과정까지 일사천리로 완료. 다음날 운좋게도 같은 설치기사님 배정. 설치과정에서도 장판걸림이 있어서 시간이 소요되긴 했으나 제품의 수평맞춤에 중점을 두고 다행이도 설치까지 완료. 좁은 공간이었지만 설치할수 있었음. 설치비용이 추가로 들지는 않았음. 첫날 통세척을 한번 해주고 다음날 오전 그릇과 냄비 수저 등을 테트리스로 잘 쌓은뒤에 프로쉬올인원 태블릿 세제를 절반으로 잘라서 표준코스와 열풍건조60분으로 함께 설정해서 시작. 완료뒤에는 순조로이 세척이 잘 되었고 약간의 흰 물얼룩이 있으나 개념치 않을 정도였으며, 다만 냄비가 완전히 뉘여져 있지 않아서인지 약간의 음식물 자국이 남아있었음. 그릇배열의 노하우가 생기면 괜찮아지지 않을까 생각함. 설치시 린스사용과 정제소금관련 설명을 들어보았기에 차후에 시도해보면서 비교해야할것같음. 6개월 케어쉽 프로그램도 참여중인데 어떨지 기대가 됨. 설거지 노동이 줄어들것으로 기대되는 식기세척기.벡색가전제품에선 엘지가 가장 좋다는 믿음과 함께 오래오래 사용하길 기대중.

The sink was remodeled and prepared with another company, but the installer said that it was not a structure that could be installed, so I decided to exchange it for a 12-person freestanding. This process seemed to take time, but since the Bestshop sales staff and the installer communicated smoothly, the cancellation and repurchase process were completed quickly. The next day, luckily, the same installer was assigned. The installation process also took time because the floorboard was jammed, but fortunately, the installation was completed with a focus on leveling the product. It was possible to install it even though it was a small space. There was no additional installation cost. I washed it once on the first day, and the next morning, I stacked dishes, pots, and spoons with Tetris, cut the Prosh All-in-One tablet detergent in half, set it to the standard course and hot air drying for 60 minutes, and started. After completion, it washed smoothly and there were some white stains, but they were not noticeable. However, there were some food stains because the pot was not completely laid down. I think it will be okay once I get the know-how to arrange the dishes. Since I heard an explanation about the use of rinse aid and refined salt during installation, I think I will have to try it out later and compare. I am also participating in the 6-month care ship program, so I am looking forward to it. A dishwasher that is expected to reduce the amount of work required to wash dishes. I believe that LG is the best in white home appliances and I look forward to using it for a long time.
Comments (Original): 식기세척기 처음으로 구매해본 후기. 베스트샵에서 식기세척기 관련 친절한 설명과 함께 진행했던 구매시간. 가격차이가 얼마나지 않고 몇가지 할인이 좋아서 14인용 빌트인으로 정했음. 싱크장은 다른업체와 개조를 완료하고 준비하였으나 설치기사님 왈 설치불가한 구조이기에 12인용 프리스탠딩으로 교환하기로 함. 이 과정에 시간이 걸리는듯 하였으나 베스트샵 판매직원분과 설치기사님과의 3자소통이 원활하였기에 취소부터 재구매 과정까지 일사천리로 완료. 다음날 운좋게도 같은 설치기사님 배정. 설치과정에서도 장판걸림이 있어서 시간이 소요되긴 했으나 제품의 수평맞춤에 중점을 두고 다행이도 설치까지 완료. 좁은 공간이었지만 설치할수 있었음. 설치비용이 추가로 들지는 않았음. 첫날 통세척을 한번 해주고 다음날 오전 그릇과 냄비 수저 등을 테트리스로 잘 쌓은뒤에 프로쉬올인원 태블릿 세제를 절반으로 잘라서 표준코스와 열풍건조60분으로 함께 설정해서 시작. 완료뒤에는 순조로이 세척이 잘 되었고 약간의 흰 물얼룩이 있으나 개념치 않을 정도였으며, 다만 냄비가 완전히 뉘여져 있지 않아서인지 약간의 음식물 자국이 남아있었음. 그릇배열의 노하우가 생기면 괜찮아지지 않을까 생각함. 설치시 린스사용과 정제소금관련 설명을 들어보았기에 차후에 시도해보면서 비교해야할것같음. 6개월 케어쉽 프로그램도 참여중인데 어떨지 기대가 됨. 설거지 노동이 줄어들것으로 기대되는 식기세척기.벡색가전제품에선 엘지가 가장 좋다는 믿음과 함께 오래오래 사용하길 기대중.

Sentence (English): None of my aunties had a dishwasher, but after much deliberation, I finally bought one!
Comments (English): [ I finally got to know Aunt Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || None of my aunties had a dishwasher, but after much deliberation, I finally bought one! I was debating between the 12-place setting and the 6-place setting because the layout of my house makes it awkward to install under an induction cooktop. I ended up buying the 6-place setting, and so far, I am extremely satisfied. Because of my personality—thinking "I can just wash quickly, that’s fine"—I hadn't gotten one before, but it feels like I haven't done enough dishes. It’s incredibly convenient to wash a few extra items after a meal and then put them in. Since it was my first time, I only used detergent, but I heard that using rinse aid prevents stains, so I bought that as well. It ran for about 1 hour and 10 minutes, and the noise wasn't loud enough to be bothersome. The door opens automatically when it finishes. If I leave it running overnight, I think everything will be dry by morning. There were quite a few reviews about unfriendly technicians, but two kind technicians came for me, so I had a pleasant installation experience. ((Review after about a week of use)). Now I understand why everyone raves about the "dishwasher auntie." Why did I wait so long to buy one? It is sooooo convenient. As I wrote above, I really... I have a personality that likes to clean up quickly, so I thought a dishwasher wouldn't suit me, but I was wrong. It's so convenient. Since I use rinse aid along with it, stains don't appear at all. On the fast cycle, it runs for about 57 minutes, and the door opens automatically when there are 2 minutes left. If I run it at night and go to sleep, everything is dry by morning, which is great. When there are few dishes, I cut the detergent in half to use. It's a 6-place setting, but if you play Tetris well, a lot fits inside! If you're hesitating, I don't think you'll regret buying it. ((One-month usage review)). It's definitely a no-brainer purchase! Honestly, since this was the last dishwasher I'd ever bought, I had the mindset that I could just be faster without one. But no, Dishwasher Auntie wins! It's seriously so convenient. My child was sick during the holidays, so I stayed home for 4 days. Cooking three meals a day meant there was a constant stream of dishes to wash, but the dishwasher really did the work. All I had to do was lightly rinse out the solids with water after eating and put everything in. Once you finish, you're done, so it really doesn't even take 5 minutes. Even my child, who used to wait until I finished the dishes every time, loves it now that Mom cleans up quickly and plays with me. At first, I wondered if the noise was a bit loud, but if I put it away and do other things, it's just like everyday noise, so sometimes I can't even hear it. For those of you hesitating, don't worry and just go ahead and buy it. I really hope you experience the convenience!

Comments (English): [ I finally got to know Aunt Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || None of my aunties had a dishwasher, but after much deliberation, I finally bought one! I was debating between the 12-place setting and the 6-place setting because the layout of my house makes it awkward to install under an induction cooktop. I ended up buying the 6-place setting, and so far, I am extremely satisfied. Because of my personality—thinking "I can just wash quickly, that’s fine"—I hadn't gotten one before, but it feels like I haven't done enough dishes. It’s incredibly convenient to wash a few extra items after a meal and then put them in. Since it was my first time, I only used detergent, but I heard that using rinse aid prevents stains, so I bought that as well. It ran for about 1 hour and 10 minutes, and the noise wasn't loud enough to be bothersome. The door opens automatically when it finishes. If I leave it running overnight, I think everything will be dry by morning. There were quite a few reviews about unfriendly technicians, but two kind technicians came for me, so I had a pleasant installation experience. ((Review after about a week of use)). Now I understand why everyone raves about the "dishwasher auntie." Why did I wait so long to buy one? It is sooooo convenient. As I wrote above, I really... I have a personality that likes to clean up quickly, so I thought a dishwasher wouldn't suit me, but I was wrong. It's so convenient. Since I use rinse aid along with it, stains don't appear at all. Cooking three meals a day meant there was a constant stream of dishes to wash, but the dishwasher really did the work. All I had to do was lightly rinse out the solids with water after eating and put everything in. Once you finish, you're done, so it really doesn't even take 5 minutes. At first, I wondered if the noise was a bit loud, but if I put it away and do other things, it's just like everyday noise, so sometimes I can't even hear it. For those of you hesitating, don't worry and just go ahead and buy it. I really hope you experience the convenience!

Comments (English): [ I finally got to know Aunt Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || None of my aunties had a dishwasher, but after much deliberation, I finally bought one! I was debating between the 12-place setting and the 6-place setting because the layout of my house makes it awkward to install under an induction cooktop. I ended up buying the 6-place setting, and so far, I am extremely satisfied. Because of my personality—thinking "I can just wash quickly, that’s fine"—I hadn't gotten one before, but it feels like I haven't done enough dishes. It’s incredibly convenient to wash a few extra items after a meal and then put them in. Since it was my first time, I only used detergent, but I heard that using rinse aid prevents stains, so I bought that as well. It ran for about 1 hour and 10 minutes, and the noise wasn't loud enough to be bothersome. The door opens automatically when it finishes. If I leave it running overnight, I think everything will be dry by morning. There were quite a few reviews about unfriendly technicians, but two kind technicians came for me, so I had a pleasant installation experience. ((Review after about a week of use)). Now I understand why everyone raves about the "dishwasher auntie." Why did I wait so long to buy one? It is sooooo convenient. As I wrote above, I really... I have a personality that likes to clean up quickly, so I thought a dishwasher wouldn't suit me, but I was wrong. It's so convenient. Since I use rinse aid along with it, stains don't appear at all. On the fast cycle, it runs for about 57 minutes, and the door opens automatically when there are 2 minutes left. If I run it at night and go to sleep, everything is dry by morning, which is great. When there are few dishes, I cut the detergent in half to use. It's a 6-place setting, but if you play Tetris well, a lot fits inside! If you're hesitating, I don't think you'll regret buying it. ((One-month usage review)). It's definitely a no-brainer purchase! Honestly, since this was the last dishwasher I'd ever bought, I had the mindset that I could just be faster without one. But no, Dishwasher Auntie wins! It's seriously so convenient. My child was sick during the holidays, so I stayed home for 4 days. Cooking three meals a day meant there was a constant stream of dishes to wash, but the dishwasher really did the work. All I had to do was lightly rinse out the solids with water after eating and put everything in. Once you finish, you're done, so it really doesn't even take 5 minutes. Even my child, who used to wait until I finished the dishes every time, loves it now that Mom cleans up quickly and plays with me. At first, I wondered if the noise was a bit loud, but if I put it away and do other things, it's just like everyday noise, so sometimes I can't even hear it. For those of you hesitating, don't worry and just go ahead and buy it. I really hope you experience the convenience!

Comments (English): [ I finally got to know Aunt Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || None of my aunties had a dishwasher, but after much deliberation, I finally bought one! I was debating between the 12-place setting and the 6-place setting because the layout of my house makes it awkward to install under an induction cooktop. I ended up buying the 6-place setting, and so far, I am extremely satisfied. Because of my personality—thinking "I can just wash quickly, that’s fine"—I hadn't gotten one before, but it feels like I haven't done enough dishes. It’s incredibly convenient to wash a few extra items after a meal and then put them in. Since it was my first time, I only used detergent, but I heard that using rinse aid prevents stains, so I bought that as well. It ran for about 1 hour and 10 minutes, and the noise wasn't loud enough to be bothersome. The door opens automatically when it finishes. If I leave it running overnight, I think everything will be dry by morning. There were quite a few reviews about unfriendly technicians, but two kind technicians came for me, so I had a pleasant installation experience. ((Review after about a week of use)). Now I understand why everyone raves about the "dishwasher auntie." Why did I wait so long to buy one? It is sooooo convenient. As I wrote above, I really... I have a personality that likes to clean up quickly, so I thought a dishwasher wouldn't suit me, but I was wrong. It's so convenient. Since I use rinse aid along with it, stains don't appear at all. ((One-month usage review)). It's definitely a no-brainer purchase! Honestly, since this was the last dishwasher I'd ever bought, I had the mindset that I could just be faster without one. Cooking three meals a day meant there was a constant stream of dishes to wash, but the dishwasher really did the work. All I had to do was lightly rinse out the solids with water after eating and put everything in. Once you finish, you're done, so it really doesn't even take 5 minutes. At first, I wondered if the noise was a bit loud, but if I put it away and do other things, it's just like everyday noise, so sometimes I can't even hear it. For those of you hesitating, don't worry and just go ahead and buy it. I really hope you experience the convenience!

For those of you hesitating, don't worry and just go ahead and buy it. I really hope you experience the convenience!

For those of you hesitating, don't worry and just go ahead and buy it. I really hope you experience the convenience!

For those of you hesitating, don't worry and just go ahead and buy it. I really hope you experience the convenience!

Sentence (English): But no, Dishwasher Auntie wins!
Comments (English): [ I finally got to know Aunt Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || None of my aunties had a dishwasher, but after much deliberation, I finally bought one! I was debating between the 12-place setting and the 6-place setting because the layout of my house makes it awkward to install under an induction cooktop. I ended up buying the 6-place setting, and so far, I am extremely satisfied. Because of my personality—thinking "I can just wash quickly, that’s fine"—I hadn't gotten one before, but it feels like I haven't done enough dishes. It’s incredibly convenient to wash a few extra items after a meal and then put them in. Since it was my first time, I only used detergent, but I heard that using rinse aid prevents stains, so I bought that as well. It ran for about 1 hour and 10 minutes, and the noise wasn't loud enough to be bothersome. The door opens automatically when it finishes. If I leave it running overnight, I think everything will be dry by morning. There were quite a few reviews about unfriendly technicians, but two kind technicians came for me, so I had a pleasant installation experience. ((Review after about a week of use)). Now I understand why everyone raves about the "dishwasher auntie." Why did I wait so long to buy one? It is sooooo convenient. As I wrote above, I really... I have a personality that likes to clean up quickly, so I thought a dishwasher wouldn't suit me, but I was wrong. It's so convenient. Since I use rinse aid along with it, stains don't appear at all. On the fast cycle, it runs for about 57 minutes, and the door opens automatically when there are 2 minutes left. If I run it at night and go to sleep, everything is dry by morning, which is great. When there are few dishes, I cut the detergent in half to use. It's a 6-place setting, but if you play Tetris well, a lot fits inside! If you're hesitating, I don't think you'll regret buying it. ((One-month usage review)). It's definitely a no-brainer purchase! Honestly, since this was the last dishwasher I'd ever bought, I had the mindset that I could just be faster without one. But no, Dishwasher Auntie wins! It's seriously so convenient. My child was sick during the holidays, so I stayed home for 4 days. Cooking three meals a day meant there was a constant stream of dishes to wash, but the dishwasher really did the work. All I had to do was lightly rinse out the solids with water after eating and put everything in. Once you finish, you're done, so it really doesn't even take 5 minutes. Even my child, who used to wait until I finished the dishes every time, loves it now that Mom cleans up quickly and plays with me. At first, I wondered if the noise was a bit loud, but if I put it away and do other things, it's just like everyday noise, so sometimes I can't even hear it. For those of you hesitating, don't worry and just go ahead and buy it. I really hope you experience the convenience!

Comments (English): [ I finally got to know Aunt Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || None of my aunties had a dishwasher, but after much deliberation, I finally bought one! Because of my personality—thinking "I can just wash quickly, that’s fine"—I hadn't gotten one before, but it feels like I haven't done enough dishes. It’s incredibly convenient to wash a few extra items after a meal and then put them in. Since it was my first time, I only used detergent, but I heard that using rinse aid prevents stains, so I bought that as well. It ran for about 1 hour and 10 minutes, and the noise wasn't loud enough to be bothersome. The door opens automatically when it finishes. For those of you hesitating, don't worry and just go ahead and buy it. I really hope you experience the convenience!

For those of you hesitating, don't worry and just go ahead and buy it. I really hope you experience the convenience!

Sentence (English): Overall a good dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Good but with some issues ] || ---------------- || Overall a good dishwasher. Very quiet and dishes turn out clean. The rack is well laid out and the water bottle jet is a nice feature to have. However, it has some design quirks/build quality issues. The lower rack is very hard to slide in/out since the silverware basket, once clipped onto the rack, will rub the door seal. It seems the gap between the right edge of the lower rack and the right door rubber seal is not wide enough to compensate for the additional space of the silverware clips. Also the tracks on the door are not aligned perfectly with the tracks inside the dishwasher, making the matter even worth. The steam feature is only for sanitization cycle and is not used for cleaning as in some other brands. I also wish there are places to hold chopsticks/straws: the clips on the 3rd rack trays are too narrow and the holes on the silverware basket bottom are too big.

Sentence (English): Upgraded from a dependable 10 year old plastic tub Whirlpool dishwasher to this steel tub one, and love it- it's so quiet I forgot I was doing a load of dishes, and the metal interior dries things (esp plastics) much better than the old one.
Comments (English): Upgraded from a dependable 10 year old plastic tub Whirlpool dishwasher to this steel tub one, and love it- it's so quiet I forgot I was doing a load of dishes, and the metal interior dries things (esp plastics) much better than the old one. I absolutely love the third rack and use it for things like serving/cooking spoons, large knives and flat cheese graters. Every new dishwasher is a learning curve of how to most efficiently load it, and I feel like I have more options with the tines on this one, which I like. Cleans dishes well even when I use cheaper store brand detergent pods, and it even does a pretty good job on crusty baked on stuff, which I usually try to pre soak. As long as Whirlpool keeps making dependable dishwashers, I'll stick with them!

Sentence (English): We've had this new dishwasher for three months.
Comments (English): [ Good dishwasher for the price ] || ---------------- || We've had this new dishwasher for three months. It replaced a 5 year old Whirlpool after the motherboard failed. We normally use the one hour quick wash and the dishes do come out clean. It is a bit noisier than the Whirlpool. Ordering, delivery and installation was easy. Costco two year warranty was a definite plus. Third rack is nice for small plates, bowls and utensils. It seems to hold more than the Whirlpool. Generally, it seems cheaply constructed with many plastic parts. Have had some issues with the upper spray arm disconnecting from the upper rack and the lower rack repeatedly getting off track. A lot of wash/dry options that we'll probably never use. Overall, I'm satisfied with it, my wife not as much as I am. It will be interesting to see how long this one lasts. For us, we'd have been happier with a cheaper model with less bells and whistles but this one was good for the price.

Sentence (English): This is my first time buying a dishwasher.
Comments (English): This is my first time buying a dishwasher. Compared with many products, Haier W30 is the most cost-effective one in the same price range. At first, I was worried that there would be water accumulation when drying with the door open. Now I tried the dishwashing beads and added the disinfection function, and the inner wall was very dry after washing! As long as it is placed properly, it can clean away old oil stains and there will be no odor in the cabin after washing. Especially when people come to eat, twenty or so dishes are really a good thing to free your hands. The installation master is also very patient. He has reserved a place in advance and will help you adjust it to a satisfactory height and stuff it into the cabinet perfectly.

Sentence (English): We recently purchased this dishwasher a couple of weeks ago and we are very sad we went with this model.
Comments (English): [ Worst Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || We recently purchased this dishwasher a couple of weeks ago and we are very sad we went with this model. This dishwasher doesn't hold as many dishes (because of the tine placement and the utensil rack not on the door) so we are having to do more washes which eliminates the energy efficiency of the product. The dishes, though they are more spaced out) do not come clean. We have gone through the manual and tried some of the trouble shooting and it hasn't helped. Our old dishwasher required no trouble-shooting it just washed the dishes that you put in it even if they had food on them. This dishwasher requires way more scraping and cleaning and there is still food marks on the dishes that rub off with the touch of a finger when the cycle is done. The lights on the door are so bright you can hardly read the numbers and time left. The one upside is that the fingerprint stainless steel is great and it is nice looking but if you want more than looks in a dishwasher, I would recommend looking at a different model or brand.

Sentence (English): One month in and happy with the dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ A nice upgrade with useful design features ] || ---------------- || One month in and happy with the dishwasher. Replaced a 24 yo Whirlpool Gold that was going strong but time to retire. We chose this 204 model to get a high end, low noise unit but in white, which limited our choices as stainless is ubiquitous and exclusive in the 404/604 models. It was well priced for Black Friday and included a free install. The design matches our 3 yr old double oven unit. We have had good luck with whirlpool/kitchen aid brands for decades, but we will see about this unit. We like the size and operation - it is easier to load than other brands we looked at or have used elsewhere in our travels. Plenty of headroom for our larger dishes and we can load two rows of cereal bowls in middle drawer. Dishes come out very clean. Comments (English): [ It's a cost-effective ODM product from a major company, so I can't not buy it! ] || ---------------- || The dishwasher I'd had at home for over 10 years broke. It was already a product that brought me so much happiness, so I loved it, but in a fit of rage, I bought it. I hadn't thought much about it, so I initially planned to order from a well-known brand. But a friend who uses the internet a lot told me that dishwashers are often ODMs, except for certain brands, and that I should just buy a good, value-for-money product. So I looked into it and found that a brand I always trust was selling this product as an ODM, so I ordered it right away. It was about half the price. At first, I was worried about the high installation costs, but luckily, I ordered it the next day through Coupang Rocket Installation without hesitation. I was also more careful and thorough than anyone else. Some people say they buy hundreds-dollar items based solely on reputation, but I bought it on impulse. I wanted to find a good product at a low price so I wouldn't regret my decision. The more I looked into it, the more I realized how cost-effective it was! Everyone says hot air drying isn't necessary because of the electricity bill, so I looked for a product that simply opens the lid. It was exactly what I wanted: thorough cleaning, an automatic door opening, and, best of all, about half the price of other products. I didn't even hesitate an hour before ordering. Since my previous dishwasher was for 12 people, I ordered a 12-person size. I simply removed the old one and installed it, so the installation process wasn't too long. They even took the old one with them, so I didn't have to worry about disposing of it, and it was easy to dispose of. I was wondering why I bought it in black. I wanted to order it in gray, but now that it's installed, black doesn't look bad either! Since my refrigerator is black, I made a good choice. I was excited to turn on the dishwasher, and it cleaned all the stuck-on rice, chili powder, and meat grease, which was a delight! It's not too noisy, and the included cutlery holder is spacious. It's a great deal! Plus, Coupang offers a two-year warranty, so I trust them more than any other company! I've always been satisfied with Coupang's service, so I think this aspect was a huge help in my decision! It doesn't dry as perfectly as a hot air dryer, but it doesn't smell or retain moisture! Thanks to this, I feel like I got a great product at a great price with free installation! I think this will be the best purchase I made this year!
